critiques: Curriculum B offers a much more logical pedagogical progression. It starts with the core concept of Pivot Tables (which also introduces slicers), moves to Lookups, then Pivot Charts, and finally ties everything together in the Dashboard build. Curriculum A introduces slicers on regular tables before teaching pivot tables or lookups, which disrupts the learning flow. Both curricula respect the language, time budget, and 25-minute-per-video constraints perfectly, but Curriculum B's structure makes it the better choice for a beginner.

Both curricula perfectly match the learner's constraints: they use Hindi-language videos, keep every single video under the 25-minute limit, and respect the overall 90-minute budget. They both also successfully teach the required lookup functions, pivot tables, pivot charts, and tie it all together with a dashboard project. Curriculum A is slightly better structured, as it integrates the concept of slicers directly into its comprehensive pivot table and dashboard tutorials rather than dedicating a standalone video to table slicers like Curriculum B does, making it a more efficient path to the exact same goal.

Curriculum A is a well-structured, logical progression that directly addresses the learner's goal. It covers slicers, VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP, pivot tables, pivot charts, and concludes with a full, 22-minute project building a sales dashboard, keeping all videos within the 25-minute constraint. Curriculum B, on the other hand, is highly redundant, repeating beginner pivot table introductions four times and lookup tutorials four times, while completely failing to include a dashboard project or layout instruction.

Curriculum A is a collection of redundant videos, repeating basic Pivot Table and VLOOKUP tutorials multiple times without ever progressing to the learner's actual goal of building a dashboard. Curriculum B is perfectly structured for the learner's goal and constraints: it covers foundational topics like turning raw data into tables and using VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, then moves logically through pivot tables, pivot charts, and culminates with a comprehensive project building a monthly sales dashboard. All videos in B are under the 25-minute limit and in Hindi, respecting all constraints while preventing wasted time on duplicate content.

Curriculum A provides a much better logical progression for a beginner. It dedicates solid, distinct blocks of time to each foundational skill (VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, Pivot Tables, Pivot Charts, and Slicers) before culminating in a single, comprehensive 22-minute dashboard build. Curriculum B, on the other hand, crams Pivot Charts and Slicers into a single 4-minute surface-level video and then spends over 40 minutes on two back-to-back dashboard projects. Both curricula respect the 25-minute per video constraint and the Hindi language requirement, but Curriculum A's pacing and structure will be much more effective for learning the individual mechanics before combining them into a dashboard.

Curriculum B provides a much stronger, logical progression without redundancy. It starts by teaching how to convert data into an Excel Table (a crucial step for dashboards), builds up lookup skills, introduces pivot tables and charts systematically, and ends with a single, comprehensive dashboard project. Curriculum A, by contrast, spends over 40 minutes on two back-to-back dashboard builds, which is redundant and leaves out dedicated instruction on converting raw lists to tables.
